title: Evening bug digest + perf TODOs (scratchpad)
content:
Quick evening dump — mix of confirmed issues, experiments to run tomorrow, and tiny reminders I don’t want to forget. Mostly raw, will tidy later when I have time.

Top priorities (by impact):
- P1: intermittent 99p spikes on nvme-backed nodes (customer hit tonight). Need repro and spike attribution. Suspect KV-cache churn + async writeback.
- P2: two failures in nightly perf-run A (seq_len 2048) — hangs at token 142 across multiple runs. Looks like attention kernel stall.
- P3: API-level 502 for small requests during autoscaler events — suspect race where connection pool drains early.

Notes / quick evidence:
- 99p spike trace (from prod span): 
  - route: /v1/generate (hosted-us-west)
  - trace snippets: large tail latencies align with KV miss rate bump (+18% misses in 5m window) and a backlog increase on the batching queue (queue_depth peaked at 340).
  - logs: saw multiple "kv-cache: eviction triggered" messages from worker-3 ~22:18 PST.

- Nightly perf hang (perf-run-A): 
  - run id: perf-A-20260310-02
  - failing model variant: redwood/gpt2x-optim-8bit
  - stack snapshot: worker thread stuck in attention cuda kernel, last host log before hang: "kv_cache_sync: flushing 1 shards".
  - hypothesis: cache flush triggered I/O and blocked kernel launch on same stream causing deadlock; need to verify stream usage and cudaEvent waits.

Repro steps to run tomorrow (short checklist):
1) Reproduce 99p spike locally with loadgen: use sample distribution skewed to long-tail sequences (80% short, 20% >1500). Run against nvme instance with same config as prod (test-ami-202602).
   - command: ./tools/loadgen --config tests/late-tail.yaml --target-host 10.2.4.8 --concurrency 400 --duration 15m
2) Enable verbose kv-cache logs for worker-3 process only (env: KV_CACHE_LOG_LEVEL=debug) and collect kernel timing (nvprof/nvtx) for the hung run.
3) Small repro harness for attention stall: run looped generation with deterministic seeds and force a cache flush at N=120 to see if it stalls.

Immediate mitigation ideas (fast followers):
- Reduce default kv-cache eviction aggressiveness for nvme nodes (config: kv_cache.eviction_threshold: 0.85 -> 0.95). Quick canary on canary pool.
- Add small backoff between cache flush and kernel launch (bad but quick). Prefer to audit stream usage first.
- Autoscaler: mark draining nodes to delay connection pool close until in-flight batches are empty.

Tasks for tomorrow (ordered):
- [ ] Reproduce spike locally (loadgen) and attach trace logs (Riley)
- [ ] Run nvprof on hung variant and capture CUDA stream timeline (Diego)
- [ ] Triage autoscaler 502 reproducibility (Aisha) — collect access logs around scale events
- [ ] PR to add per-worker kv-cache debug endpoint (simple /debug/kv-status) returning small metrics (me/maybe later)
- [ ] Add gating in autoscaler: wait-for-empty-batches flag (small change in pool-drain logic)

Open questions / unresolved things:
- Why does eviction spike correlate with long-tail load specifically on nvme? Is NVMe throughput the bottleneck or is it metadata locking? Need iostat and fio runs to verify.
- Is the attention kernel stall happening only on 8-bit quantized models? Need to test float16 variant to rule out quantization path bug.
- Are there cross-worker locks when we flush cache shards? Look for cross-process file locks or redis rpush/pop patterns.

Short logs/snippets pulled from prod tonight (redacted):
- "[22:18:03] worker-3 kv_cache: eviction triggered (size=298MB -> 260MB)"
- "[22:18:07] worker-3 kernel: launch attention_optim_stream:0 status=queued"
- "[22:18:07] worker-3 kernel: attention_optim_stream:0 status=running"
- "[22:18:12] worker-3 kv_cache: flush complete (shard=17)"
- "[22:23:19] nginx: 502 upstream prematurely closed connection"

Quick commands / env notes:
- To increase kv logs for just worker-3: KUBECTL: kubectl -n serving exec deploy/worker-3 -- bash -c "export KV_CACHE_LOG_LEVEL=debug; kill -HUP 1"
- Kernel profiling: run inside pod with nsys: nsys profile --output=profile-$(date +%s) --trace=cuda --sample=none --openmp=none --duration=60 -- python -m serve.bench attention_hang_test.py
- Simple fio baseline (run on nvme node): fio --name=kv-meta --iodepth=64 --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=2G --runtime=120 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1

Notes to ping people:
- @aisha: can you pull autoscaler logs and check scale events between 22:10-22:30 PST? Need the graceful drain timing.
- @diego: can you run nvprof on the hung variant tomorrow AM and capture stream events? Put results in /mnt/tmp/profiles/ so I can grab.
- @product: should we notify the handful of affected customers? —> probably wait until we have mitigation that reduces 99p by >30%

Small UX/housekeeping todos:
- move nightly perf-run-A to use new CI node label to avoid noisy prod-like interference (jenkins job update)
- add short note to runbook: "if 99p spikes and kv-cache eviction messages appear, temporarily set eviction_threshold to 0.95 and monitor"

Evening brain dump ends here. Will convert into a short incident doc if repro confirmed. Low priority: refactor metric names to be more explicit (kv_cache.* vs cache.*) — sounds trivial but will help future signal-to-noise.

-- Riley
